EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East situation remains volatile, dominated by ongoing US-Iran "deep talks" and a fragile ceasefire, which President Trump has given a short deadline before threatening renewed "powerful military action." This diplomatic window is complicated by escalating Houthi drone attacks on Saudi Arabian oil facilities and Iran's vow of "regret-inducing" retaliation against Ukraine for a Caspian Sea ship attack, indicating a high risk of renewed and expanded regional conflict.

IRAN
Diplomatic efforts with the US are ongoing, described by President Trump as "deep talks" facilitated by mediators including Qatar, Pakistan, and Oman. Trump warned of a short negotiation window, threatening "powerful military action" if talks fail, while Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Ismail Baghaei, denied direct negotiations but confirmed message exchanges via mediators. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi recounted rejecting US "extremist requests" during talks in Islamabad, including a demand for the southern Strait of Hormuz route to be active.

In the Strait of Hormuz, Iran intercepted six vessels attempting to use an "unauthorized route" in the southern part of the strait, with one vessel reportedly "suffering an incident." Iran has accused the US of using commercial ships for military purposes in the Strait. The IRGC spokesperson, Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi, stated that Hormuz played a role in Iran's deterrence strategy and that Iran "did not get tricked" by the ceasefire, but used the opportunity. CNN reported that nearly all vessels have been using Iran's designated route through the Strait. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper reportedly recommended halting US bombing around Hormuz due to its effectiveness reaching limits.

Iran has vowed a "regret-inducing" response to Ukraine's drone attack on the Iranian commercial vessel 'Anna' in the Caspian Sea, which reportedly killed a sailor named Nima Moradi. Iranian officials, including the Foreign Ministry, IRGC spokesperson, Ambassador to Russia Kazem Jalali, and MP Ebrahim Azizi, condemned the attack as a "criminal act" and "illegal." Ukraine, conversely, claimed Iran had already attacked it by supplying drones to Russia since 2022.

Internally, four members of the PJAK terrorist group were killed in the Baneh border area, western Iran. An Iranian opposition Kurdish group in Erbil (Koysanjak) also reported a drone attack. The Iranian Army pledged a strong response to any future aggression. The IRGC spokesperson claimed US bases suffered "huge damage" and US forces were "rendered blind" by Iranian attacks, reducing their operational power.

Economically, Iran is facing electricity shortages for industries, with 400 megawatts of additional power allocated to industrial parks and new power plants expected to supply industries by late summer/early fall. Gasoline prices have reportedly increased to 10,000 Toman per liter. The Central Bank governor claimed inflation was halved in July. Tehran's Prosecutor General filed charges against a former MP and a media outlet.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations in Gaza included the killing of Amro Abu Alrish, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) Nochuva terrorist involved in the release of an Israeli hostage, in the southern Gaza Strip. In northern Gaza, Abd Al-Nasser Al-Aziz Maqadmeh, a commander in Hamas's police and a deputy platoon commander in its military wing, was also killed. Additionally, Wael al-Ladawi, the commander of Hamas's internal security forces in the central Gaza Strip, was killed in a strike in Deir al-Balah. The IDF also demolished a Hamas tunnel spanning hundreds of meters in northern Gaza. Near the Jordan border, the IDF intercepted two drones that did not cross into Israeli territory; their origin is under investigation.

In the West Bank, Israeli forces, including the IDF, Border Police, and Shin Bet, arrested four individuals involved in the theft of a soldier's weapon in Sussya, south of Hebron. Over 130 wanted individuals were also arrested across the West Bank, including Hamas operatives, weapons dealers, and those planning immediate attacks. The house of a terrorist involved in a recent Friday attack was sealed, and another mapped. Entry of Palestinian workers into settlements has been blocked until Tuesday.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu departed for Washington to meet President Trump, his first White House meeting in five months, with Iran as the primary agenda. Netanyahu stated his goal is to "safeguard our security while also expanding the circle of peace around us." His office moved a cabinet meeting to an undisclosed underground location, citing security concerns over a potential Iranian threat. Israel Katz will fill in for Netanyahu in Cabinet meetings, and Yariv Levin for government meetings. Former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett vowed to declare Qatar an "enemy state" if re-elected, accusing it of funding Iran's Revolutionary Guards and Hamas. The Religious Zionism party held primaries, with Orit Strock, Simcha Rothman, Zvi Sukkot, and Ohad Tal elected as the top four after party leader Bezalel Smotrich. The Attorney General is seeking a court order to prevent the implementation of a new law regarding the Police Internal Affairs Department (Machash).

On the home front, an IDF drone was found in Kibbutz Nahal Oz, with no security incident reported. A fire in the Sha'ar HaNegev industrial zone was brought under control. An ammonia leak and fire in Sderot (Strauss and Tapugan factories) led to the evacuation of the surrounding industrial area. Two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossed the border into Syria near Mount Hermon, marking the seventh such incident in a month; the IDF condemned the act and called for legal prosecution.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In Gaza, ground operations included the IDF demolition of a Hamas tunnel, hundreds of meters long, in the northern Strip. Targeted strikes by the IDF killed Amro Abu Alrish, a PIJ Nochuva terrorist involved in a hostage release, in southern Gaza, and Abd Al-Nasser Al-Aziz Maqadmeh, a Hamas police commander, in northern Gaza. Wael al-Ladawi, commander of Hamas's internal security in central Gaza, was also eliminated in a strike in Deir al-Balah. The humanitarian situation saw a report of a pregnant Palestinian woman losing her fetus after her ambulance was delayed at an Israeli checkpoint. Ceasefire and negotiation status in Gaza are unclear, with Prime Minister Netanyahu stating he would oppose US demands for a broad Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, Syria, and Lebanon. Settler activity was noted with two Israeli settlement activists illegally crossing into Syria from the Mount Hermon area.

LEBANON
No direct Hezbollah operations were mentioned in the raw intelligence. However, Israeli forces shelled areas in southern Lebanon, specifically targeting the outskirts of the Ali al-Taher Heights in the Nabatieh region. Omid Dana reported powerful Israeli attacks on villages of Br'ashit, Bint Jbeil, Aitaroun, Al-Tiri, and Mays al-Jabal in southern Lebanon. During IDF operational activity in the village of al-Taybeh in southern Lebanon, two drawings of Adolf Hitler were found in a private house, reportedly part of a school operating under Hezbollah's auspices. No UNIFIL incidents were reported. Displacement figures were not available. Lebanon's President condemned ongoing Israeli violations, reaffirming adherence to the framework agreement but rejecting continued breaches. Lebanese Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri reaffirmed his opposition to direct negotiations with Israel. A Lebanese lawmaker from the Amal Movement stated that any agreement with Israel would be "meaningless" without a complete withdrawal of Israeli occupation forces from southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Saudi Arabia's Defense Ministry claimed that drones targeting its eastern oil facilities and Riyadh were launched from Iraq by "Iran-backed militias." This led to a Saudi Foreign Ministry statement condemning the attacks and requesting Iraq prevent its territory from being used as a launchpad. In Iraq, a US-made Lucas drone (MQ-4C) crashed in Babil province, with no reported damage, though images showed a large explosion. There were also reports of a drone attack on a US base in Erbil. Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is scheduled to visit Turkey after recent visits to Iran and the United States. In Syria, President Ahmed Al-Shar'a stated Damascus is working with several countries towards a security agreement with Israel, hoping for "comprehensive peace" while preserving Syria's rights over the Golan Heights. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres reaffirmed the Golan Heights as Syrian territory and urged an end to Israeli violations.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's Defense Ministry announced the interception of several drones targeting oil facilities in the eastern region and Riyadh, attributing them to "Iran-backed militias" in Iraq and reserving the right to respond. The Foreign Ministry condemned these attacks and urged Iraq to prevent its territory from being used for such actions. Yemeni Houthis claimed responsibility for drone attacks on Saudi oil depots and pipelines, specifically mentioning Ras Tanura, Yanbu, Abqaiq, and Jazan, in response to Saudi drone incursions into Yemeni airspace. Satellite imagery showed fires and smoke plumes at Abqaiq and Jazan facilities. One report also suggested a 50% drop in Saudi oil exports due to Houthi blockade efforts, impacting 3-4 million barrels per day.

Oman's Foreign Minister, Bader Al-Busaidi, engaged in telephone calls with regional counterparts to discuss de-escalation and stressed the importance of political and diplomatic understandings to ensure maritime security in the Strait of Hormuz. Oman is also identified as a key mediator in the ongoing US-Iran talks. Qatar's Foreign Ministry condemned the drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities. However, former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett threatened to declare Qatar an "enemy state" if re-elected, accusing it of funding Hamas and Iran's Revolutionary Guards. Kuwait's army issued a recruitment call following "Iran attacks on US bases" in Kuwait, with an investigation piece from Press TV suggesting Kuwait and Bahrain may have "miscalculated by becoming launchpads for US strikes on Iran." Politico reported a consensus among Gulf states on ending the war and keeping Hormuz open, but disagreements on the approach, with Oman and Qatar favoring negotiation, UAE a tougher stance, and Saudi Arabia a middle ground.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Iran Diplomatic Engagement and Ultimatum**: President Trump confirmed "deep talks" with Iran through mediators (Qatar, Pakistan), but issued a strict deadline for negotiations, threatening "powerful military action" if they fail. Iran confirmed message exchanges but denied direct talks.
2.  **Escalating Houthi Attacks on Saudi Oil Infrastructure**: Yemeni Houthi forces claimed drone attacks on multiple Saudi Arabian oil facilities, including Ras Tanura, Yanbu, Abqaiq, and Jazan. Saudi Arabia confirmed intercepting drones, attributing them to Iran-backed militias in Iraq, and reserved the right to respond. Satellite images showed significant fires at Abqaiq and Jazan facilities.
3.  **Iran's Vow of Retaliation Against Ukraine**: Iran's Foreign Ministry and IRGC spokesperson warned of a "regret-inducing" response to Ukraine's drone attack on the Iranian commercial vessel "Anna" in the Caspian Sea, which reportedly killed an Iranian sailor. Ukraine countered that Iran had already attacked it by supplying drones to Russia since 2022.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Confrontation**: Iran's IRGC intercepted six vessels attempting to use an "unauthorized route" through the Strait of Hormuz, with one reportedly "suffering an incident." This followed Iran's warnings against US use of commercial ships for military purposes.
5.  **Targeted Israeli Strikes in Gaza**: The IDF conducted precise strikes, killing Amro Abu Alrish (PIJ Nochuva terrorist involved in a hostage release), Abd Al-Nasser Al-Aziz Maqadmeh (Hamas police/military commander), and Wael al-Ladawi (Hamas internal security commander in central Gaza). A Hamas tunnel in northern Gaza was also demolished.
6.  **Israeli Prime Minister's US Visit**: Benjamin Netanyahu traveled to Washington to meet President Trump, with Iran as the primary agenda, aiming to discuss Israeli security and expanding peace.
7.  **West Bank Security Operations**: Israeli forces arrested four individuals involved in a weapon theft from a soldier in Sussya and detained over 130 wanted individuals across the West Bank, including Hamas operatives and those planning immediate attacks.
8.  **Syrian President Expresses Interest in Israeli Security Agreement**: Syrian President Ahmed Al-Shar'a stated efforts are underway to achieve a security agreement with Israel, involving several countries, aiming for comprehensive peace while upholding Syria's rights over the Golan Heights.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation between the US and Iran is critically high, as President Trump's ultimatum for "deep talks" expires quickly, threatening a return to "powerful military action." The Strait of Hormuz remains a severe flashpoint, with Iran's interception of vessels and accusations against the US increasing the potential for direct confrontation over crucial global oil transit routes. A new front of conflict could open with Iran's explicit threat of retaliation against Ukraine for the Caspian Sea ship attack, potentially drawing in Russia. Regional instability is heightened by continued Houthi drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities and Saudi Arabia's attribution of these to Iran-backed militias in Iraq, carrying a significant risk of wider regional conflict. In Gaza and the West Bank, targeted Israeli strikes against Hamas and PIJ commanders, coupled with extensive arrest operations, indicate persistent, intense conflict with no signs of de-escalation. Furthermore, the Shin Bet chief's warning about Iranian attempts to interfere in upcoming Israeli elections highlights an emerging cyber and political threat vector.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture is dominated by President Trump's statements confirming "deep talks" with Iran but also threatening "powerful military action" if negotiations fail swiftly. Trump rejected reports of munitions shortages and asserted the US possesses ample military resources. The Pentagon updated its casualty database for the Iran war to 642 killed or wounded under a new "Overseas Operations" category. Trump also dismissed Netanyahu's opposition to F-35 sales to Turkey, noting Turkish President Erdoğan as a friend, and questioned Ukrainian President Zelensky's claim about Russian provision of satellite images to Iran. CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper reportedly recommended halting the US bombing campaign around the Strait of Hormuz, citing that its effectiveness had reached its limits.

Among the **Gulf States**, Saudi Arabia condemned drone attacks originating from Iraq and reserved the right to respond forcefully, urging Iraq to prevent its territory from being used for such actions. Oman's Foreign Minister engaged in regional consultations focused on de-escalation and the importance of securing maritime navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar also condemned the drone attacks on Saudi facilities. Kuwait issued a military recruitment call following reported "Iran attacks on US bases" in the country. Gulf states generally agree on the necessity of ending the conflict and keeping Hormuz open but diverge on the best diplomatic or military approach.

**EU members** expressed concerns over potential new US trade tariffs. France and Spain received emergency aid, including aircraft, helicopters, and firefighting teams from other EU nations, to combat massive wildfires.

**Russia's** Kremlin warned that Ukraine's attacks in the Caspian Sea were "very dangerous." Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova cautioned the UK against deploying Gripen fighter jets to Ukraine, threatening a similar fate to other Western military equipment. Iran's ambassador to Russia stated that Iran expects a "serious response" from Russia regarding the attack on the Anna vessel.

**China's** Commerce Ministry accused the US of "AI hegemony" and threatened countermeasures following US warnings to Chinese AI companies over alleged technology theft.

**Turkey** is set to host Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi following his visits to Iran and the US.

Other notable international developments include Chad and Venezuela announcing their withdrawal from the International Criminal Court, citing an "excessive focus on African nations." Colombian President-elect Avelardo de la Esperilla announced plans to move Colombia's embassy to Jerusalem, halt the establishment of a Palestinian embassy, and close several other diplomatic missions as part of a reform effort. UK legislators called for a comprehensive arms embargo and a ban on trade supporting illegal settlements against Israel. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres reaffirmed the Golan Heights as Syrian territory and urged Israel to cease sovereignty violations.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions persist in the reporting regarding US-Iran interactions. While President Trump publicly stated "deep talks" are underway and that mediators requested a pause in US strikes, Iran's Foreign Ministry denies any direct negotiations, only acknowledging message exchanges through intermediaries. This discrepancy could be a deliberate strategy by Iran for internal political consumption or a genuine distinction in diplomatic engagement levels, but it creates ambiguity around the actual state of play.

Claims of casualties and damage are heavily contested. The US Pentagon updated its database to show 642 US forces killed or wounded in the Iran war, under a new "Overseas Operations" category. Conversely, IRGC spokesperson Brigadier General Hossein Mohebbi alleged over 200 US troops were killed, accusing US officials of lying and targeting civilian infrastructure in Iran. These figures from both sides are likely subject to propaganda and lack independent verification.

The attribution of drone attacks on Saudi Arabia remains ambiguous. Saudi Arabia asserts these drones originated from "Iran-backed militias in Iraq" and has explicitly called on Iraq to prevent its territory from being used. However, Press TV dismisses these Saudi claims as unverified. Meanwhile, the Houthis claimed responsibility for the attacks, stating they were in response to Saudi drone incursions into Yemeni airspace. The actual chain of command and launch origins require further clarity.

Details surrounding Iran's interception of six vessels in the Strait of Hormuz are also vague. While Iran reported one vessel "suffering an incident," no further details or independent corroboration are available regarding the nature or severity of this incident.

Political framing is evident in various statements, such as former Israeli Prime Minister Naftali Bennett's declaration to designate Qatar as an "enemy state" if re-elected, based on accusations of funding the IRGC and Hamas. This stance, while presented as intelligence-based, is likely influenced by Israeli internal politics and efforts to leverage regional tensions.

Reporting gaps include a lack of specific information on the "incident" involving the vessel in Hormuz, the precise circumstances and detailed impact of the US drone crash in Babil province, and independent verification of the full extent of damage to Saudi oil facilities beyond satellite imagery. The political backing and broader activities of the "Bashan Pioneers," Israeli settlement activists who repeatedly cross into Syria, are also not fully detailed, beyond the IDF's condemnation of their actions.
